text: A `.class` file contains machine code for the processor that compiled it.
explanation: It contains bytecode for the Java Virtual Machine — a stack machine defined by a specification document rather than by silicon, with around 200 opcodes and no general-purpose registers. That is why the same `.class` file runs on an Intel laptop and an ARM server. Chapter 21 shows four of those opcodes doing real work: the distinction between `invokestatic`, `invokespecial`, `invokevirtual` and `invokeinterface` is exactly the distinction between the kinds of dispatch.
